page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The modified organ
lines: Leaves are modified to trap insects.
These plants grow in nitrogen-poor soils and
digest the trapped insects for their nitrogen
steps.why: The organ is the LEAF, and the reason is nitrogen - the soil lacks it, so the plant digests insects to get it.
common_mistakes: Writing stem or root as the trapping organ. The trap is always a modified leaf.
Saying the plant eats insects for energy. It still photosynthesises; the insects supply nitrogen.
steps.memory_tip: Leaf traps, nitrogen is the prize.
steps.margin_note: Organ + the nitrogen line; the reason is part of the mark.

steps.label: Two examples
steps.why: Two named genera with the shape of each trap show the examiner you know the modification, not just the plant names.
common_mistakes: Misspelling the genera - Nepenthes and Dionaea (the book prints 'Dionea').
steps.memory_tip: A pitcher that pours and a trap that snaps - Nepenthes and Dionaea.
steps.margin_note: Genus + common name each; the trap shape is a bonus line.
